business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Catalog Retail of Industrial Maintenance Hardware

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction; Panama City Public Registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified) with Anglo-American commercial and fiduciary law adaptations; Private Interest Foundations governed by a bespoke statute combining elements of the common-law trust and the civil-law foundation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 11 May 1991)
Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (FTA, in force 31 October 2012)
Panama-Singapore Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (in force 2008)
Panama-United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (entered into force 2013)
Panama-Luxembourg Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (entered into force 2013)
Panama-Qatar Agreement on Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force 2013)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS (Panama joined 20 January 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework implementing FATF Recommendations) as amended; Executive Decree No. 49 of 2 July 2015 (regulatory due-diligence and beneficial-ownership rules); Law 70 of 30 January 2019 and Executive Decree No. 218 of 2020 (Beneficial Ownership Registry administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos, MEF); Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations as amended by Law 12 of 2010; Executive Decree No. 312 of 2 July 2020 (economic substance rules for foundations) ; Resolution No. 01/2015 rules of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Instrumento de Fundación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Circuit Notary executing the public deed; foreign founder executes via certified Power of Attorney before a notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (foreign executed signature); Apostille through Dirección de Legalizaciones y Apóstillas of the Panamanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs for local notarial instruments

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's Power of Attorney to execute the Foundation Charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of origin of the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and, where the source state is not party to the Apostille Convention, full consular legalization at the Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (Certificación de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Resident Agent / Founding Council Secretary of the foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized Panamanian instrument followed by Apostille for onboarding with foreign custodial banks; administrative copy filed with the DGI UBO Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of corporate founder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of the founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of founders, council members and beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree No. 49 of 2015 for all founders, foundation council members, protectors and beneficiaries: (i) screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, World-Check/Refinitiv high-risk country matrix and domestic Panamanian public integrity registers; (ii) determination of Politically Exposed Person status (domestic/international PEPs, immediate family members and close associates per FATF Recommendation 12); (iii) verification of source of funds and source of wealth for the initial foundation endowment; (iv) mandatory filing of Suspicious Transaction Reports (ROS) with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) where any red flag arises; (v) resident agent retention of AML/CFT files for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Online Name Reservation Module (Ventanilla de Consultas / Reserva de Nombre) at www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must incorporate the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' and may be expressed in Spanish, English or another language using Latin script; non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration; the proposed name must not be identical, phonetically equivalent or confusingly similar to any existing company, foundation or trademark registered in Panama; the name must not contravene public order, public morals or statutory naming prohibitions; all registry records and certificates are issued in Spanish with an optional English translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bank / Banking (prior Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá approval)
Seguros / Reaseguros / Insurance / Reinsurance (prior insurance sector supervisory approval)
Trust / Fiduciario / Fiduciary (prior Fiduciary authority license)
Fondo de Inversión / Investment Fund (prior securities market regulatory authorization)
Bolsa / Exchange / CBC (prior Panama Stock Exchange or securities regulator clearance)
Cooperativa / Cooperative (prior national cooperative authority approval)
Ministerio / Gobierno / República / Nacional / Municipal (reserved for state or public institutions)
Any term constituting offensive, scandalous or criminally suggestive expression
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant files a written 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five business days of notification, presenting an alternative distinguishing element, additional disclaimer or evidence of prior trademark authorization; if administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may initiate an annulment action ('demanda contencioso-administrativa') before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months; alternatively, the reservation may be re-filed after the 30-day validity window with a materially distinguishable name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office in Panama at the physical situs of its licensed resident agent (an authorized Panamanian attorney or law firm) or another verifiable physical address located in Panama; pure virtual-office addresses, PO boxes or mail-forwarding services are not acceptable as the statutory seat; however, operational staff and e-commerce business functions may be fully remote while the resident agent's address satisfies the legal presence requirement; a municipal Aviso de Operación is not required if no Panama-sourced commercial activity is conducted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5%) within the first 24 months for an inactive or offshore-source PIF with no Panamanian taxation nexus and no municipal operating license; probability rises to an estimated 15-25% upon opening a Panamanian bank account, registering with the DGI for municipal/tax purposes, or invoking economic substance in Panama; unannounced inspections may be conducted by DGI, UAF, the Public Registry, or municipal authorities under their statutory inspection powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley 21 de 2017, Articles 3, 12, 15, 16, 20 and 34; Código de Procedimiento Registral (Ley 18 de 2006); Ley General de Ambiente No. 41 de 1998 for environmental attributes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva / Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter / Foundation Deed), duly notarized and inscribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Ley 25 de 1995 does not mandate a statutory minimum endowment; however, the Foundation Charter must declare an initial patrimony appropriate to the foundation's purpose. Recommended and market-standard paid-up endowment: USD 10,000, evidenced by a bank certificate, asset valuation, or founder's written declaration. No escrow account is required under Panamanian law; capital may be contributed in cash, goods, or rights.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL. The undersigned council members, convened pursuant to Article 15 of the Charter, resolve: (1) the USD 10,000 initial endowment declared by the Founder is acknowledged, fully subscribed, and irrevocably dedicated to the foundation's purpose; (2) the registered office is fixed at the Resident Agent's offices in Panama City; (3) Roberto Vargas, Susan Chen, and the Resident Agent are appointed as President, Secretary-Treasurer, and Resident Agent respectively, each accepting the appointment and vested with full administrative powers within the Charter's scope. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Resident Agent and Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney acting as Agente Residente (Resident Agent) under Ley 25 de 1995
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the resident agent with founder and beneficial owner details, chosen foundation name, corporate purpose (electronic catalog B2B retail of industrial MRO supplies), council composition, asset provisions, and registered office. The resident agent must confirm name availability at the Public Registry and draft the bilingual Spanish/English Foundation Charter.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder passport or national ID
Signed formation instruction letter with corporate purpose
Bank reference letter or proof of funds statement
Name availability search request with three alternate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is unavailable or registry query is raised, revise the Charter, select an alternate name, and re-file through the resident agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Panamanian public notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent coordinates execution of the final Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary. The notary reads the instrument, verifies the identity and legal capacity of the founder and founding council members, authenticates the signatures, and issues the first protocol copy together with notarized copies for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Final draft Foundation Charter
Passport copies of all signatory parties
Official notarial duty stamps
Resident agent acceptance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial objection is raised, clarify any conflicting clauses, amend the Charter paragraph, and re-execute the instrument before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter, the registry application form (SIR/F-01), the resident agent's power of attorney, and proof of payment of the B/.150 official registration fee to the Public Registry. Upon successful review, the Registry assigns a Ficha de Fundación and issues the Certificado de Fundación de Interés Privado registrado.
required_dossiers: Notarized original and first copy of the Foundation Charter
Registry application form SIR/F-01
Resident agent power of attorney
Registry fee payment receipt (USD 150)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a nota de defecto, file a correcting instrument (Acta de Corrección y Aclaración) through the resident agent within 15 business days; if denied, pursue judicial appeal under Articles 120-125 of Ley 18 de 2006.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting and Adoption of Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (Consejo Fundacional) and, if appointed, the Protector under the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council, adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, approve internal regulations, establish banking signatory authority, approve the B2B e-commerce policy, and maintain a book of resolutions. Minutes are notarized and, when third-party effects are sought, subsequently inscribed at the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Notice of council meeting
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Letter accepting appointment from officers and resident agent
AML/KYC identity dossier of council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment is challenged or stalemate occurs, convene an extraordinary council session; if required, amend the Charter via an Acta de Reforma and register such amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Commercial Operation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía de Panamá – Administración Municipal de Rentas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC registration with the DGI for the foundation to obtain a tax identification number and to support bank account opening. Obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación for the commercial/warehouse activity if physical premises are used. Confirm the territorial taxation posture: foreign-source income of the PIF remains outside Panamanian income tax; ITBMS is not applicable to qualifying exports of goods or services.
required_dossiers: Certified note or registration certificate from the Public Registry
RUC registration form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
Copy of the resident agent license and registered office evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the Municipality queries the application, correct the activity classification to NAICS 423840 / ISIC 4791 and submit a clarifying sworn affidavit; appeal administrative refusals through the Conciliation and Tax Appeals channels of the DGI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Verificación Comercial
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Registro Industrial para Depósito y Venta al por Mayor de Suministros Industriales de Mantenimiento (MRO), issued under Ley 23 de 2007 and applicable municipal regulations of Alcaldía de Panamá.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Administración Regional de Panamá
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (Registro Ambiental de Bajo Impacto) per Ley No. 41 de 1998 and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 57 de 2004; no full EIA study required for a non-manufacturing, low-impact warehouse and e-commerce distribution facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to public sewer must satisfy Decreto Ejecutivo No. 17 de 2009 (MINSA) and MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0291-2016 indicative limits (pH 6.0-9.0, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L). Airborne VOC emissions from storage of lubricants, solvents, and aerosol MRO products must comply with COPANIT ambient air quality standards and applicable best available control technology (BACT) practices. Hazardous maintenance residues (used oils, batteries, contaminated PPE, aerosols) must be transported and disposed by MiAMBIENTE-registered handlers, with hazardous waste manifests retained for five years.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety certificate covering emergency exits, extinguishers, rack sprinkler arrangements, and electrical load inspection; MIVIOT (Ministerio de Vivienda y Ordenamiento Territorial) structural load assessment for storage racks; and MITRADEL occupational health clearance verifying workplace signage, PPE availability, and ergonomic standards for warehouse staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), Republic of Panama. Online portal: Sede Digital / https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or Panama Private Interest Foundation obtains a single RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) by filing foundation charter, public deed, by-laws, resident agent appointment certificate, field inspection forms, and any required DGI applications. The DGI must verify the physical or registered address, then issue a provisional RUC followed by a definitive RUC within the statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Panama law. A Private Interest Foundation may, however, elect the simplified Small Taxpayer regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) for qualifying local activities, and under Law 61 of 2021 may elect the special e-commerce regime subject to DGI certification and compliance requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBM – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT-like transfer tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (USD 36,000) in annual gross taxable sales or services; foreign digital suppliers may have narrower registration triggers under Law 61 of 2021
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates DGI-approved electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) with phased implementation. Covered taxpayers must use a certified fiscal invoicing system that transmits each invoice and credit note in real time to the DGI electronic clearing platform, applies a digital signature and unique confirmation code, and generates the required QR code prior to delivery of the document to the buyer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT/ITBM (0%) applies to commercial export sales of tangible goods that physically depart Panamanian customs territory, and to certain offshore B2B services where the service is rendered and used outside Panama, provided the seller has a valid RUC, invoices under Panama tax rules, and retains export contracts and proof of foreign receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Aduanera de Exportación)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (B/L or AWB)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Collection Evidence (Swift or credit-dated remittance)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and Panama Customs (Aduanas) jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate physical exit or collection within the 180-day repatriation period triggers reversal of the zero rate and collection of the omitted ITBM at 7%, plus statutory surcharges and interest. Intentional false declarations expose the taxpayer to minimum fines of 100% of the omitted tax, administrative penalties, and criminal tax evasion prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá); Panama has no central bank, with Banco Nacional de Panamá acting as the state-owned fiscal agent and government treasury service provider.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy without a domestic central-bank issued currency. The Panamanian balboa (PAB) exists only as a nominal unit of account pegged at 1:1 to the U.S. dollar, and USD is legal tender throughout the Republic. There are no foreign exchange controls, no restrictions on capital account or current account transactions, no prior central bank authorizations, and no limits on dividend or profit repatriation from a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation. All ordinary B2B MRO catalog sales proceeds may be received in USD or any freely convertible foreign currency, and retained offshore or in Panamanian banks without forced conversion. Profit remittance to non-resident foundation beneficiaries is restricted only by AML/KYC documentation requirements, not by exchange control regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not impose any statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation timelines. Exporters and e-commerce operators, including a Private Interest Foundation, may retain all export earnings in foreign currency and deploy capital and profits freely through the international banking system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Panama has adopted Law 75 of 2019 and the Superintendency of Banks' Regulatory Agreement for Innovation, but there is no comprehensive licensed electronic money institution (EMI) regime equivalent to the European Electronic Money Directive. Offshore digital EMIs domiciled in the UK, EU, or other jurisdictions are not recognized for Panamanian clearing, cannot open local settlement accounts without a Panamanian banking license, and may be treated as unregulated payment processors. They are viable as supplementary collection rails only, and must be supplemented by the foundation's own bank account at a Panamanian commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, most Panamanian tier-1 banks require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner to appear physically at a bank branch for a compliance interview and to provide original identification documents. Some institutions permit remote account opening for non-resident clients using apostilled or notarized copies and videoconference interviews, but this is granted only on a case-by-case basis and often requires endorsement from the licensed resident agent or an attorney-in-fact in Panama. A fully remote account opening without any Panama connection is generally not possible for high-quality commercial banking relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation lacks demonstrable commercial substance, physical office, or operational expenses, causing red flag for shell-company risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation charter and public deed; Foundation Council resolution approving bank account opening and operating mandate; resident agent certificate in good standing; physical or virtual office lease agreement in Panama; e-commerce platform infrastructure documentation; logistics and supplier contracts; and a certified 12-month business plan with projected transaction volumes and source-of-wealth narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire remittances from multiple third-party payers do not match named counterparties on MRO supply invoices, triggering suspicion of trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and commercial invoices; shipping bills of lading or forwarder cargo receipts; customs broker documents; payment reconciliation ledger matching each SWIFT MT103 reference to an underlying receivables entry; and a written explanation of intercompany or reseller arrangements, if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or appointed Foundation Council member appears in adverse media, sanction lists, or politically exposed persons (PEP) databases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent compliance report from a licensed Panamanian due-diligence firm; notarized source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for the foundation corpus and operating capital; original bank statements from the funding account; negative PEP screening results from reputable databases such as World-Check or LexisNexis; and, where applicable, an explanation of any benign PEP association.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Credit-card and payment-processor settlements intended for B2B MRO sales show consumer-typical credit card deposits in high-volume or high-frequency patterns, triggering unusual activity surveillance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original merchant acquiring agreement or payment service provider (PSP) registration showing settlement instructions into the foundation's Panamanian bank account; processing fee invoices; chargeback and refund policies; compliance declarations confirming digital sales are business-to-business transactions; and monthly order and revenue reports with issuer bank details for end-user corporate purchasers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial capital injection into the Private Interest Foundation, use a SWIFT MT103 wire from the funding institution (typically the founder's personal or corporate bank) to the beneficiary account at a Panamanian commercial bank. The wire must include the Foundation's legal name, foundation identification number, account number, and a clear purpose code such as 'CAPITAL INCREASE' or 'SUBSCRIPTION OF FOUNDATION ASSETS'. The instruction must be supported by a notarized capital subscription resolution of the Foundation Council, a letter of instruction signed by the registered council, and evidence of the founder's legal identity and tax status. Inbound B2B trade receipts must use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TRADE PAYMENT' or 'GOODS AND SERVICES', and include the relevant invoice number and purchase order reference to permit straight-through processing and audit traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound vendor and transportation payments should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for regular wire settlement, with explicit invoice reference and ISIC business description. For high-value industrial MRO goods and Chinese or Korean exporter requirements, use documentary commercial letters of credit issued in USD, typically communicated via SWIFT MT700/MT707, with UCP600 compliance. Where counterparties accept open account terms, settlement may also be routed through Panamanian correspondent banks using local USD clearing (ACH/CHIPS) and backed by freight and customs documentation. All outbound payments must be matched against an approved vendor registry, and each disbursement above the internal threshold should require dual authorization by the Foundation Council and the appointed treasury officer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on major convertible pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CNY/USD) transacted through a Panamanian licensed bank or a recognized international broker
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American restricted currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Brazilian real) permitted for non-resident foundations hedging dividend or trade receivable exposures
Cross-currency swaps on USD/EUR or USD/CNY pairs, executed with a licensed counterparty under ISDA documentation
FX options and currency swaptions for prudent treasury management where the counterparty is a regulated Panamanian bank or an international dealer operating under the Panama Securities Market law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax ('Impuesto de Franquicia') — Ley 25 de 1995, Art. 9 (flat annual foundation tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP) / Dirección General de Ingresos; collection via Banco Nacional de Panamá, Caja de Ahorros, or ANIP e-payment portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 30 June of every calendar year; permissible payment window from 1 January to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% statutory surcharge for payments made 1 July–31 August; 15% surcharge from 1 September onward; delinquent PIF recorded in ANIP's 'en mora' register, denied Paz y Salvo certificates; Public Registry of Panama rejects all foundation filings (amendments, transfers, agent changes) until tax plus surcharges settled; no automatic strike-off applies to PIFs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return ('Declaración de Renta') — applicable only if the PIF earns Panamanian-source income or carries on business in Panama (territorial taxation: foreign-source profits excluded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ANIP / Dirección General de Ingresos (national electronic filing platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the foundation's fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end: 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory surcharge and 1% monthly interest per Código Fiscal Arts. 728–733; ANIP may issue an ex officio assessment ('determinación de oficio'), register the PIF as a non-filer, and enforce collection with embargoes on bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO / Due-Diligence File Refresh — 'Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final' addressed to the Resident Agent (Ley 23 de 2015, Art. 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent (private regulated subject under supervision of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero — UAF, and the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the foundation's registration in the Public Registry of Panama; additionally, written UBO update must be delivered within 30 days of any change in beneficiaries, Foundation Council members, or protector
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Resident Agent: fines up to USD 100,000 and license suspension under Ley 23 de 2015 for outdated client files; Foundation: refusal of agent services, loss of good-standing certification, and de-risking or closure of banking relationships.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Public Registry — NOT REQUIRED for Panama Private Interest Foundations (no annual report, annual declaration, or shareholder list is filed; the franchise tax is the sole obligatory annual government payment for a passive PIF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable (Ley 25 de 1995 imposes no annual return filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: None — this entry documents the absence of an annual filing obligation and clarifies that non-filing cannot trigger administrative strike-off for a PIF.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit obligation exists for PIFs under Ley 25 de 1995. An independent certified audit becomes compulsory only when: (i) the foundation charter or an internal resolution of the Foundation Council expressly mandates it; (ii) the PIF carries on commercial operations in Panama and ANIP requests audited financial statements during an examination; or (iii) a lender or counterparty contractually conditions financing or commercial facilities on audited accounts (common in B2B MRO credit lines).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as endorsed by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá when formal financial statements are prepared; simplified cash-basis records are legally sufficient for a passive holding PIF with no Panamanian-source income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent must refresh the PIF's client due-diligence file at least once per calendar year (anniversary-based), and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, beneficiary designation, Foundation Council membership, or protector appointment. The Founder and Foundation Council must co-sign the annual 'Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final' identifying natural-person UBOs and source of funds; the declaration is retained by the Resident Agent and is not filed with any public register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation deed ('Escritura Pública Constitutiva') and Public Registry certificate of registration
Register of Foundation Council Members ('Registro de Miembros del Consejo')
Minute Book ('Libro de Actas') of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 1,200 per year (incl. Resident Agent service, statutory registered office, and franchise tax processing)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (no statutory audit for passive PIF) – USD 3,500 for a voluntary certified audit of a small holding PIF

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable Panama-source income of juridical persons; the reduced small-taxpayer bracket of 15% may apply only to qualifying taxpayers falling strictly under Ley 49 de 2014 regimes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: all foreign-source income is excluded from Panamanian income tax. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) that derives no Panama-source business income and conducts no commercial activity in Panama is not subject to ISR; its only fixed treasury obligation is the annual B/.300 foundation franchise tax paid to the Public Registry. Qualifying free-zone activities, Colon Free Zone operations, and internationally licensed logistics/port services may benefit from special statutory regimes, but a pure B2B MRO e-commerce operator with foreign fulfillment and customers qualifies only for the foreign-source exclusion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 230 — Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta for juridical persons; filed electronically through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-filing portal (T@ss / Portal de Declaraciones) using the taxpayer RUC and authorized digital credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the standard Panamanian fiscal year is the calendar year. Taxpayers must also make monthly advance ISR payments through the monthly withholding/advance declaration mechanism, but the annual Formulario 230 is the definitive return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year; DGI may grant no extension by default unless a formal arrangement is made before the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross receipts: gross proceeds from industrial MRO catalog sales, commissions, logistics services and other business activity where the contract is concluded, the goods are delivered, or the economic use/exploitation occurs in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source revenue. Foreign e-commerce orders fulfilled from foreign warehouses to non-Panama customers are outside the territorial scope and should not be reported in this line even if collected through a Panama payment-acceptance account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt foreign-source income: gross receipts from foreign business operations, foreign bank deposits, foreign-issued IP royalties, and foreign e-commerce catalog sales where all operational management, contracting, fulfillment, and title transfer occur outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed foreign-source income schedule, bank statements from the foreign sales accounts, warehouse or drop-shipping contracts, and delivery documentation to substantiate the foreign sourcing. Do not net foreign losses against Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions directly attributable to Panama-source income: purchases of MRO inventory, warehousing, shipping, sales commissions, chargeback losses, and operating expenses that are ordinary and necessary for the production of Panama-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only costs with proper invoice support and clear allocation to Panama-source revenue. Foreign central costs and IP acquisition costs should be allocated conservatively using documented apportionment keys and maintained in the DGI file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Panama-source gross receipts less allocable deductions; if the result is negative, enter zero and carry the loss forward for five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with zero Panama-source activity should file a nil return and expressly state that all income is foreign-source. Losses may not be created from foreign-source operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISR payable: apply the 25% corporate rate to net taxable income; subtract valid prepayments and tax credits; remit the resulting balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If related-party transaction adjustments apply, increase taxable income by the transfer pricing adjustment before computing tax. Where the Impuesto Empresarial de Tasa Única (IETU) regime applies to active Panama operations, pay the greater of ISR or the 4.67% unified-rate minimum on gross revenue, as applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-payment attract a 10% late-filing surcharge on the tax due plus 1% monthly interest on unpaid amounts. DGI may additionally impose administrative fines of approximately B/.100 to B/.10,000, block RUC operations, estimate tax by internal audit, and institute criminal tax proceedings for willful failure to file or false filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding applies to dividends or profit distributions made by a Panamanian entity out of Panama-source taxable profits. Distributions paid from foreign-source profits are outside the territorial tax base and should not be subject to withholding if the foreign-source character can be demonstrated.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where an applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) is in force, the non-resident payee must deliver a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority, together with a declaration of beneficial ownership, supporting substance documents, and a duly legalized Spanish translation where required. The Panamanian withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate at source only when the TRC and DGI relief forms are current; otherwise tax is withheld at the statutory rate and the payee may apply to DGI for refund under the applicable treaty administrative procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for the use of IP in Panama are subject to gross-basis withholding of 12.5%; interest paid to non-residents on financing effectively used in Panama is subject to 6% withholding. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10% and interest to 5%, while interest on financing deployed exclusively outside Panama is not Panama-source and is not subject to withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama's transfer pricing law and implementing regulations require the Local File (and, where applicable, Master File) when the taxpayer's annual gross revenue exceeds B/.2,500,000 or the taxpayer engages in related-party transactions exceeding B/.1,000,000 in a fiscal period; Master File documentation is additionally required where the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue exceeds B/.13,000,000. The local currency is the Panamanian balboa (B/.), pegged at par to the U.S. dollar.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Panamanian Economic Substance Regulations (Ley 254 de 2021 and implementing rules) require entities carrying on relevant activities, including holding/managing assets, distribution and service centers, and headquarters, to demonstrate adequate employees, physical premises, and board management in Panama. A PIF engaged as a pure B2B MRO e-commerce operator through foreign fulfillment, foreign bank accounts, and foreign customers must maintain substance documentation showing management outside Panama or otherwise justify non-residence; if it holds Panama operating assets or earns Panama-source income, it must file the annual economic substance report. Failure to do so can create a statutory shell-company presumption and trigger substantial penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF conducts an active industrial MRO catalog distribution business with Panamanian warehouse inventory, Panamanian delivery, or repeated Panamanian customers, but does not obtain a RUC, does not register with DGI, files a nil return, or excludes Panama-source revenue from Formulario 230.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may issue a tax assessment based on bank deposits and reconstructed sales, charge the 25% ISR plus 10% late-payment surcharge and 1% monthly interest, impose fines of up to B/.10,000, and refer the case to the Public Prosecutor for tax fraud. Criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of two to five years and financial penalties of up to approximately B/.50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and the protector who sign or knowingly approve false tax returns become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, surcharges, and interest. Criminal proceedings may also trigger preventive seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and judicial orders prohibiting departure from Panama pending final sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Misstatement of Foreign-Source Margins
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF books artificially low prices on related-party purchases from offshore suppliers, allocates excessive management or IP fees to the foreign entities, or reports a thin operating margin in Panama despite a robust catalog sales business, thereby shifting Panama-source profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the transactional price, make a primary or secondary adjustment to the Panama taxable income, apply the 25% corporate rate to the upward adjustment, and charge late-payment interest. Administrative penalties may include 40% of the understatement for consecutive non-compliant years and cancellation of the right to carry losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute intercompany contracts with non-arm's-length pricing or destroy transfer pricing documentation can be held personally liable for the resulting assessment. The courts may pierce the foundation veil, authorize attachment of directors' personal bank accounts, and order individual travel prohibitions where the transfer pricing scheme was used to facilitate tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF has no independent foundation council, holds no documented meetings, has no physical office or bank records, uses nominee directors without instructions, and merely holds contracts or IP invoices without real commercial activity, leading the tax authority to characterize it as a sham or conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's legal entity regime permits judicial disregard of the juridical personality, nullification of the foundation's protected patrimony, and recharacterization of the PIF as transparent for tax purposes. DGI may assess the founder personally on the foundation's worldwide income and impose fines under ESR for failure to file substance documentation, including penalties per annum and dissolution of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the foundation council are civilly liable to creditors for failure to exercise real control; they may also face criminal liability for aiding the unlawful use of a legal entity. Judges may order personal restitution of diverted MRO sale proceeds, issue travel bans for persons participating in sham administration, and impose imprisonment of up to seven years for fraudulent insolvency or abuse of limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Violations / Money Laundering Through MRO E-Commerce Receipts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF is used as a pass-through for revenue from fraudulent MRO procurement schemes, undisclosed beneficial owners, shell-supplier invoices, or credit-card/SWIFT wire proceeds that are withdrawn or distributed for the benefit of hidden principals without conducting customer due diligence or maintaining a suspicious-transaction file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015, together with the Financial Information and Reporting Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero), authorizes severe administrative penalties, including fines of up to B/.1,000,000 per infraction, closure of accounts, revocation of the PIF's registration, and criminal prosecution for money laundering with sentences of five to twelve years of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members, protectors, and beneficial owners who control the accounts or direct the transfers are personally subject to forfeiture of all proceeds, criminal fines, and imprisonment. Directors may be barred from holding banking or corporate positions, subjected to passport seizure and Interpol red notices, and ordered to make full civil restitution to the harmed commercial counterparties.
